To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a complementing approach for robot ethics can be developed by grounding ethics in practical robot use and that the resulting set of ethical issues can be used to inform the design of care robotics.

(1) the ethical issues that arise in the context of care robotics are different than what is commonly discussed in the literature; (2) the issues are not necessarily related to the risk of robots replacing human care workers; and (3) the issues can be addressed by designing robots that are sensitive to human concerns

1) the use of robotics in care giving may lead to a number of ethical issues that are overlooked in current ethical discussions of care robotics, and 2) that the use of robotics can be designed to address ethical issues such as increased isolation of care recipients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to make robotics a force for good in care.
the ethics of robotics as a practical matter and as a way to inform future design and development of robots.
how robotics can be developed to support the elderly and disabled in their daily life, but also with the ethical implications of such development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the robot ethics literature has not yet fully captured all the ethical issues that are likely to be raised in the future by care robots.
the use of care robots in the home setting is ethically acceptable if it is carefully designed and developed to address the identified issues.
robot ethics should not be based solely on theoretical considerations but should also include empirical data from the use of robots in practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
robotics has a potential for positive impact on care, but only if it is designed and developed with a careful consideration of the users’ needs and values.
robot ethics needs to be complemented by empirical studies of the use of robots in practice to reveal new issues and provide actionable guidance for robot design.
robotics can contribute positively to care, but only if it is designed and developed to support the care recipients’ needs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

empirical work with robotics can reveal ethical issues that are not obvious in theoretical discussions of robot ethics, and that such empirical work can provide actionable guidance for current robot design.
empirical studies of robotics in practical use can reveal new ethical issues that are overlooked in theoretical discussions.
the use of robotics in the care context is a complex and multi-faceted matter.
